name: Build desktop apps

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    tags:
      - "v*"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: desktop-build-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}

jobs:
  test-platforms:
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.name }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Linux x64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
            timeout_minutes: 25
          - name: macOS arm64
            runner: macos-15
            timeout_minutes: 25
          - name: macOS x64
            runner: macos-15-intel
            timeout_minutes: 25
          - name: Windows x64
            runner: windows-2025
            timeout_minutes: 45
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout_minutes }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install pinned Rust toolchain (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.96.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --profile minimal --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

      - name: Install pinned Windows cross toolchain (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install 1.96.1 --profile minimal --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          cargo install cargo-xwin --locked --version 0.23.1
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends clang-18 lld-18 llvm-18

      - name: Compile-check Windows helper with cargo-xwin (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: npm run build:windows-helper

      - name: Install pinned Rust supply-chain gates (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.2
          cargo install cargo-deny --locked --version 0.20.2

      - name: Install Electron binary (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: npx install-electron --no

      - name: Validate Windows managed process helper
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true
          python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --no-input Flask==3.1.0 fastapi==0.128.0 uvicorn==0.40.0
          cargo fmt --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
          cargo clippy --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --locked --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings
          cargo test --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          cargo audit --file native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.lock --deny warnings
          cargo deny --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --config native/windows-managed-process-helper/deny.toml --locked check
          npm run check:windows-helper-reproducibility
          $env:PI_WINDOWS_HELPER_HANDLE_LOOPS = "100"
          npm run test:windows-managed-helper
          npm run test:managed-process-workflows
          $env:PI_MANAGED_FLOOD_DURATION_MS = "60000"
          $env:PI_MANAGED_FLOOD_PROCESSES = "8"
          $env:PI_MANAGED_FLOOD_STREAMS = "both"
          npm run test:managed-process-flood

      - name: Run unit and handler tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Run cross-platform quality checks (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          npm run format:check
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
          npm run check:dependencies
          npm run check:contract
          npm run check:pi-compat
          npm run check:toolchain-contract
          npm run check:toolchain-catalog
          npm run check:browser-i18n

  windows-frameworks:
    name: Windows managed framework acceptance
    runs-on: windows-2025
    timeout-minutes: 35

---
type: guide
title: Development and Verification Guide
description: How to develop, build, test, verify, package, and release Pi Agent Desktop, including the verify gate, the unit test runner, and the CI pipeline.
tags: [development, build, test, verify, packaging, ci]
---

# Development and Verification Guide

This guide covers the development, verification, and packaging workflows for Pi Agent Desktop. Treat the source of each script as authoritative; the `verify` sequence below is the pre-commit/pre-pack gate.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22.19.0 or higher, below 23 (`engines` field in `package.json`), and npm.
- A supported OS (macOS, Windows, or Linux). Platform-specific builds (Windows helper, macOS signing) require their native platform or the documented cross toolchain.

## Development loop

`npm run dev` runs `scripts/dev.mjs`, which orchestrates three processes (`scripts/dev.mjs:85-112`):

1. an initial `scripts/build-main.mjs` build of main/preload/host (must succeed before continuing);
2. `tsup --watch` (main/preload/host rebuilds) and Vite (renderer) in parallel;
3. Electron with `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:5173` once Vite is ready.

`dev.mjs` waits for Vite to answer on port 5173 (30 s timeout) and tears down every spawned child with `terminateProcessTree` on exit (`scripts/dev.mjs:12-33`, `dev.mjs:39-44`).

## Build pipeline

- `npm run build` → `scripts/build.mjs`: on Windows x64 it first builds the Rust managed-process helper, then `scripts/build-main.mjs` (tsup), then `vite build` (`scripts/build.mjs:14-18`).
- `scripts/build-main.mjs` cleans `out/main` and `out/preload` and runs tsup with `tsup.config.ts` (`scripts/build-main.mjs:11-26`).
- `tsup.config.ts` produces:
  - `out/main/main.js` — Main process, CJS, platform node, target node22, external `electron`/`electron-updater` (`tsup.config.ts:15-35`);
  - `out/main/agent-host.mjs`, `plugin-worker.mjs`, `managed-process-worker.mjs` — ESM (the pi packages only export an `import` condition), external to the `@earendil-works/pi-*` packages and `silk-wasm` (`tsup.config.ts:36-68`);
  - `out/preload/preload.js` — CJS, platform browser, target es2022 (`tsup.config.ts:69-85`).
- The build fails unless `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` is an exact version dependency; it is injected as `process.env.PI_DESKTOP_EXPECTED_PI_VERSION` via a define (`tsup.config.ts:6-13`, `vite.config.ts:13-27`).

## Unit tests

`npm test` runs `scripts/test.mjs`, which delegates to `scripts/test-runner.mjs` (`scripts/test.mjs:1-12`). The runner:

- executes `node --test src/**/*.test.mjs` with a per-test timeout (`PI_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 120 000 ms) (`scripts/test-runner.mjs:18-35`);
- rejects legacy test-bundle usage and cleans `.artifacts/test-modules` before and after (`scripts/test-runner.mjs:37-56`).

## The verify gate

`npm run verify` → `scripts/verify.mjs` runs, in order, and aborts on the first failure (`scripts/verify.mjs:21-42`):

1. `format:check` (prettier)
2. `lint` (eslint, `--max-warnings=0`)
3. `typecheck` for both `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.renderer.json`
4. `check:dependencies` (dependency contract)
5. unit tests (`npm test`)
6. managed-process development workflows
7. managed-process 60 s flood
8. contract coverage (`check-contract-coverage.mjs`)
9. Pi 0.84 compatibility
10. toolchain contract safety
11. toolchain catalog verification
12. Browser i18n invariants
13. desktop security invariants (`check-desktop-security.mjs`)
14. build (`npm run build`)
15. production artifact isolation
16. Electron smoke test
17. Browser Electron integration
18. Browser real Agent E2E

This is the same gate that `package-desktop.mjs` runs before packaging (`scripts/package-desktop.mjs:26-31`).

## Checks and acceptance suites

- `npm run smoke` launches a real Electron instance in a temp user-data dir, connects to the Host over MessagePort, and verifies ping, sessions, worktree conflict handling, git status, directory watching, exact binary download, and safe skill editing (`scripts/smoke-electron.mjs:1-60`).
- `npm run test:browser-electron` / `npm run test:browser-agent-e2e` run the built-in browser integration and real-Agent browser E2E (`src/smoke/`).
- `npm run test:managed-process-workflows`, `test:managed-process-flood`, `test:managed-process-frameworks`, and `test:windows-managed-helper` exercise the managed-process lifecycle, output flood budgets, real Next/Storybook/Spring Boot cold starts, and the Windows Job helper.
- `npm run check:contract` asserts the exact API/streams/bridge/IPC coverage described in [RPC and Contract Layer](../architecture/rpc-and-contracts.md).
- `npm run check:production-artifacts` and `npm run check:desktop-security` enforce packaging and security invariants (see [Security Model](../architecture/security-model.md)).

## Packaging

`npm run pack` (`--dir`) and `npm run dist` (`--release`) run `scripts/package-desktop.mjs` (`scripts/package-desktop.mjs:9-66`):

1. `prepare-bundled-tools.mjs` prepares the bundled `rg`/`fd` core and runtime catalogs;
2. the full `verify` gate;
3. on Windows release, `verify-windows-helper-reproducibility.mjs`;
4. `electron-builder` (`--dir` or `--publish never`);
5. on Windows release, generate and verify the CycloneDX SBOM.

`electron-builder.yml` configures: ASAR packaging of `out/**`, extra resources for the signed runtime/core catalogs and bundled core tools, macOS hardened-runtime DMG+ZIP (arm64+x64), Windows NSIS x64 (unsigned, artifact named `Pi-Agent-Desktop-Unsigned-Beta-Setup`), Linux AppImage x64 with the `--appimage-desktop-launch` override, the `pi-agent-desktop` protocol, and a GitHub draft-release publisher (`electron-builder.yml:98-175`).

`npm run dist:mac:signed` and `npm run dist:mac:notarized` run `scripts/build-mac-release.mjs`, which must run on macOS and supports `--notarize`, `--arm64`, `--x64`; notarization requires Apple credentials via one of the supported env strategies (`scripts/build-mac-release.mjs:7-60`).

## CI pipeline

`.github/workflows/build-desktop.yml` runs on push to `main`, `v*` tags, and PRs:

- `test-platforms`: the unit/handler/quality matrix on Linux x64, macOS arm64, macOS x64, and Windows x64, with pinned Rust toolchains; Windows additionally runs `cargo fmt/clippy/test`, `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`, helper reproducibility, managed-process workflows, and the 60 s flood (`build-desktop.yml:22-115`);
- `windows-frameworks`: real Next/Storybook/Spring Boot framework acceptance on Windows;
- `quality` and `package`: cross-platform quality checks and packaging;
- `release-contract`, `release-macos`, `release-windows`, `release-linux`, and `release`: the signed/notarized macOS release pipeline, Windows release asset pipeline (SBOM + packaged E2E), Linux AppImage release under Xvfb, and final release aggregation (`build-desktop.yml:384-1012`).

## Related pages

- [Quickstart](../quickstart.md)
- [Windows Managed Process Helper Guide](./windows-managed-process-helper.md)
- [Desktop Shell and Lifecycle](../systems/desktop-shell-lifecycle.md)

35: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
36: pub struct Frame {
37:     pub kind: u16,
38:     pub payload: Vec<u8>,
39: }
40: 
41: fn payload_limit(kind: u16) -> Option<usize> {
42:     match kind {
43:         HOST_BOOTSTRAP => Some(MAX_BOOTSTRAP_BYTES),
44:         HOST_COMMIT
45:         | HOST_STDIN
46:         | HOST_CLOSE_STDIN
47:         | HOST_STOP
48:         | HOST_PING
49:         | HOST_SHUTDOWN
50:         | HOST_REAP
51:         | HOST_SECURE_JOURNAL_DIRECTORY => Some(MAX_CONTROL_BYTES),
52:         _ => None,
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: pub struct FrameReader<R> {
57:     input: R,
58:     expected_sequence: u32,
59: }
60: 
61: impl<R: Read> FrameReader<R> {
62:     pub const fn new(input: R) -> Self {
63:         Self {
64:             input,
65:             expected_sequence: 1,
66:         }
67:     }
68: 
69:     pub fn read(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Frame>> {
70:         let mut header = [0_u8; HEADER_BYTES];
71:         let mut offset = 0;
72:         while offset < header.len() {
73:             match self.input.read(&mut header[offset..]) {
74:                 Ok(0) if offset == 0 => return Ok(None),
75:                 Ok(0) => return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME")),
76:                 Ok(read) => offset += read,
77:                 Err(error) if error.kind() == ErrorKind::Interrupted => {}
78:                 Err(_) => return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME")),
79:             }
80:         }
81:         if &header[0..4] != b"PIMP" {
82:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
83:         }
84:         let version = u16::from_le_bytes([header[4], header[5]]);
85:         if version != PROTOCOL_VERSION {
86:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH"));
87:         }
88:         let kind = u16::from_le_bytes([header[6], header[7]]);
89:         let length = u32::from_le_bytes([header[8], header[9], header[10], header[11]]) as usize;
90:         let sequence = u32::from_le_bytes([header[12], header[13], header[14], header[15]]);
91:         if sequence != self.expected_sequence {
92:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
93:         }
94:         self.expected_sequence = self
95:             .expected_sequence
96:             .checked_add(1)
97:             .ok_or_else(|| HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"))?;
98:         let limit =
99:             payload_limit(kind).ok_or_else(|| HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"))?;
100:         if length > limit {
101:             return Err(HelperError::protocol(if kind == HOST_BOOTSTRAP {
102:                 "HELPER_BOOTSTRAP_TOO_LARGE"
103:             } else {
104:                 "HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"
105:             }));
106:         }
107:         let mut payload = vec![0_u8; length];
108:         self.input
109:             .read_exact(&mut payload)
110:             .map_err(|_| HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"))?;
111:         Ok(Some(Frame { kind, payload }))
112:     }
113: }

115: pub struct FrameWriter<W> {
116:     output: W,
117:     next_sequence: u32,
118: }

120: impl<W: Write> FrameWriter<W> {
121:     pub const fn new(output: W) -> Self {
122:         Self {
123:             output,
124:             next_sequence: 1,
125:         }
126:     }

128:     pub fn write(&mut self, kind: u16, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
129:         let max = if matches!(kind, HELPER_STDOUT | HELPER_STDERR) {
130:             MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES
131:         } else {
132:             MAX_CONTROL_BYTES
133:         };
134:         if payload.len() > max {
135:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
136:         }
137:         let length = u32::try_from(payload.len())
138:             .map_err(|_| HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"))?;
139:         let mut header = [0_u8; HEADER_BYTES];
140:         header[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"PIMP");
141:         header[4..6].copy_from_slice(&PROTOCOL_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
142:         header[6..8].copy_from_slice(&kind.to_le_bytes());
143:         header[8..12].copy_from_slice(&length.to_le_bytes());
144:         header[12..16].copy_from_slice(&self.next_sequence.to_le_bytes());
145:         self.next_sequence = self
146:             .next_sequence
147:             .checked_add(1)
148:             .ok_or_else(|| HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"))?;
149:         self.output
150:             .write_all(&header)
151:             .and_then(|()| self.output.write_all(payload))
152:             .and_then(|()| self.output.flush())
153:             .map_err(|_| HelperError::protocol("HELPER_PARENT_UNAVAILABLE"))
154:     }
155: }

215:         let mut object = json::parse(bytes)?.object()?;
216:         let value = match object.remove("sequence") {
217:             Some(Value::Integer(value)) if value >= 0 => value as u64,
218:             _ => return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME")),
219:         };
220:         if !object.is_empty() {
221:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
222:         }
223:         Ok(value)
224:     }
225: 
226:     fn stop_job(
227:         job: &Job,
228:         process_group_id: u32,
229:         mode: StopMode,
230:         sink: &EventSink,
231:     ) -> Result<&'static str> {
232:         if mode == StopMode::Graceful {
233:             sink.send_json(HELPER_STOPPING, r#"{"phase":"interrupt"}"#.into())?;
234:             let _ = win32::send_ctrl_c();
235:             if job.wait_empty(Duration::from_secs(2))? {
236:                 return Ok("CTRL_C_EVENT");
237:             }
238:             sink.send_json(HELPER_STOPPING, r#"{"phase":"terminate"}"#.into())?;
239:             let _ = win32::send_ctrl_break(process_group_id);
240:             if job.wait_empty(Duration::from_secs(3))? {
241:                 return Ok("CTRL_BREAK_EVENT");
242:             }
243:         }
244:         sink.send_json(HELPER_STOPPING, r#"{"phase":"force"}"#.into())?;
245:         job.terminate()?;
246:         if !job.wait_empty(Duration::from_millis(1_500))? {
247:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("JOB_TERMINATE_FAILED"));
248:         }
249:         Ok("JOB_TERMINATE")
250:     }
251: 
252:     fn owner_mode(sink: &EventSink) -> Result<()> {
253:         let receiver = start_control_reader();
254:         let frame = control_with_timeout(&receiver, Duration::from_secs(10))?;
255:         if frame.kind != HOST_BOOTSTRAP {
256:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
257:         }
258:         let bootstrap = Bootstrap::parse(&frame.payload)?;
259:         let owners = win32::open_owner_handles(&bootstrap)?;
260:         let job = Arc::new(Job::create(&bootstrap.job_name)?);
261:         let mut target = Target::prepare(&bootstrap, &job)?;
262:         let helper_fingerprint = win32::current_process_fingerprint(BUILD_ID)?;
263:         sink.send_json(
264:             HELPER_PREPARED,
265:             format!(
266:                 r#"{{"helperPid":{},"helperStartFingerprint":{},"jobName":{},"helperBuildId":{},"nonce":{},"hostInstanceId":{}}}"#,
267:                 std::process::id(),
268:                 super::protocol::json_escape(&helper_fingerprint),
269:                 super::protocol::json_escape(&bootstrap.job_name),
270:                 super::protocol::json_escape(BUILD_ID),
271:                 super::protocol::json_escape(&bootstrap.nonce),
272:                 super::protocol::json_escape(&bootstrap.host_instance_id),
273:             ),
274:         )?;
275:         let commit_frame = control_with_timeout(&receiver, Duration::from_secs(5))?;
276:         if commit_frame.kind != HOST_COMMIT {
277:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
278:         }
279:         let commit = Commit::parse(&commit_frame.payload)?;
280:         if commit.nonce != bootstrap.nonce {
281:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
282:         }
283:         target.resume()?;
284:         let pipes = target.take_pipes()?;
285:         let mut target_stdin = Some(pipes.stdin);
286:         let stdout_sink = sink.clone();
287:         std::thread::spawn(move || drain(pipes.stdout, HELPER_STDOUT, stdout_sink));
288:         let stderr_sink = sink.clone();
289:         std::thread::spawn(move || drain(pipes.stderr, HELPER_STDERR, stderr_sink));
290:         let owner_lost = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
291:         let watchdog_lost = Arc::clone(&owner_lost);
292:         let watchdog_job = Arc::clone(&job);
293:         std::thread::spawn(move || {
294:             if win32::wait_for_owner_loss(owners).is_ok() {
295:                 watchdog_lost.store(true, Ordering::Release);
296:                 let _ = watchdog_job.terminate();
297:             }
298:         });
299:         sink.send_json(
300:             HELPER_STARTED,
301:             format!(
302:                 r#"{{"hostInstanceId":{},"journalRevision":{}}}"#,
303:                 super::protocol::json_escape(&bootstrap.host_instance_id),
304:                 commit.journal_revision,
305:             ),
306:         )?;
307: 
308:         let mut stopped: Option<(String, &'static str)> = None;
309:         let mut root_exit_at: Option<Instant> = None;
310:         let mut root_code: Option<u32> = None;
311:         loop {
312:             match receiver.recv_timeout(Duration::from_millis(50)) {
313:                 Ok(ControlMessage::Frame(frame)) => match frame.kind {
314:                     HOST_STDIN => {
315:                         let input = Stdin::parse(&frame.payload)?;
316:                         if let Some(stdin) = target_stdin.as_mut() {
317:                             let written = stdin.write_all(input.text.as_bytes()).and_then(|()| {
318:                                 if input.append_newline {
319:                                     stdin.write_all(b"\n")
320:                                 } else {
321:                                     Ok(())
322:                                 }
323:                             });
324:                             if written.is_err() {
325:                                 target_stdin = None;
326:                                 sink.send_json(HELPER_STDIN_CLOSED, "{}".into())?;
327:                             }
328:                         } else {
329:                             sink.send_json(HELPER_STDIN_CLOSED, "{}".into())?;
330:                         }
331:                     }
332:                     HOST_CLOSE_STDIN => {
333:                         target_stdin = None;
334:                         sink.send_json(HELPER_STDIN_CLOSED, "{}".into())?;
335:                     }
336:                     HOST_STOP | HOST_SHUTDOWN => {
337:                         let stop = if frame.kind == HOST_STOP {
338:                             Stop::parse(&frame.payload)?
339:                         } else {
340:                             Stop {
341:                                 mode: StopMode::Graceful,
342:                                 source: "host".into(),
343:                             }
344:                         };
345:                         let signal = stop_job(&job, target.process_id, stop.mode, sink)?;
346:                         stopped = Some((stop.source, signal));
347:                     }
348:                     HOST_PING => {
349:                         let sequence = parse_ping(&frame.payload)?;
350:                         sink.send_json(HELPER_PONG, format!(r#"{{"sequence":{sequence}}}"#))?;
351:                     }
352:                     _ => return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME")),
353:                 },
354:                 Ok(ControlMessage::Eof) => {
355:                     owner_lost.store(true, Ordering::Release);
356:                     job.terminate()?;
357:                 }
358:                 Ok(ControlMessage::Error(error)) => return Err(error),
359:                 Err(RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => {
360:                     owner_lost.store(true, Ordering::Release);
361:                     job.terminate()?;
362:                 }
363:                 Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => {}
364:             }
365: 
366:             if root_code.is_none() {
367:                 root_code = target.exit_code()?;
368:                 if root_code.is_some() {
369:                     root_exit_at = Some(Instant::now());
370:                 }
371:             }
372:             let active = job.active_processes()?;
373:             if active == 0 {
374:                 sink.send_json(HELPER_ACTIVE_ZERO, "{}".into())?;
375:                 let exit = if let Some((source, signal)) = stopped {
376:                     format!(
377:                         r#"{{"code":null,"signal":{},"reason":"stopped","source":{}}}"#,
378:                         super::protocol::json_escape(signal),
379:                         super::protocol::json_escape(&source)
380:                     )
381:                 } else if owner_lost.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
382:                     r#"{"code":null,"reason":"host-failure"}"#.into()
383:                 } else {
384:                     format!(
385:                         r#"{{"code":{},"reason":"exit"}}"#,
386:                         root_code.map_or_else(|| "null".into(), |value| value.to_string())
387:                     )
388:                 };
389:                 sink.send_json(HELPER_EXIT, exit)?;
390:                 std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
391:                 return Ok(());
392:             }
393:             if stopped.is_some() {
394:                 return Err(HelperError::protocol("JOB_TERMINATE_FAILED"));
395:             }
396:             if root_exit_at.is_some_and(|started| started.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(1)) {
397:                 let _ = stop_job(&job, target.process_id, StopMode::Force, sink)?;
398:                 stopped = Some(("host".into(), "JOB_TERMINATE"));
399:             }
400:         }
401:     }
402: 
403:     fn reaper_mode(sink: &EventSink) -> Result<()> {
404:         let receiver = start_control_reader();
405:         let frame = control_with_timeout(&receiver, Duration::from_secs(5))?;
406:         if frame.kind == HOST_SECURE_JOURNAL_DIRECTORY {
407:             let request = SecureJournalDirectoryRequest::parse(&frame.payload)?;
408:             win32::secure_journal_directory(&request.path)?;
409:             sink.send_json(
410:                 HELPER_JOURNAL_DIRECTORY_SECURED,
411:                 r#"{"secured":true}"#.into(),
412:             )?;
413:             std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
414:             return Ok(());
415:         }
416:         if frame.kind != HOST_REAP {
417:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_INVALID_FRAME"));
418:         }
419:         let request = ReapRequest::parse(&frame.payload)?;
420:         let Some(job) = Job::open_for_reap(&request.job_name)? else {
421:             sink.send_json(HELPER_REAP_OUTCOME, r#"{"outcome":"already-empty"}"#.into())?;
422:             std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
423:             return Ok(());
424:         };
425:         let Some(owner) = win32::open_reap_owner(
426:             request.helper_pid,
427:             &request.helper_start_fingerprint,
428:             &request.helper_build_id,
429:         )?
430:         else {
431:             sink.send_json(
432:                 HELPER_REAP_OUTCOME,
433:                 r#"{"outcome":"identity-uncertain"}"#.into(),
434:             )?;
435:             std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
436:             return Ok(());
437:         };
438:         if job.active_processes()? > 0 {
439:             job.terminate()?;
440:         }
441:         if !job.wait_empty(Duration::from_millis(1_500))? {
442:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("JOB_TERMINATE_FAILED"));
443:         }
444:         win32::terminate_reap_owner(&owner)?;
445:         sink.send_json(HELPER_REAP_OUTCOME, r#"{"outcome":"removed"}"#.into())?;
446:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
447:         Ok(())
448:     }
449: 
450:     fn version_mode() {
451:         println!(
452:             r#"{{"protocolVersion":{},"buildId":{},"arch":"x64","provenance":{}}}"#,
453:             PROTOCOL_VERSION,
454:             super::protocol::json_escape(BUILD_ID),
455:             super::protocol::json_escape(PROVENANCE),
456:         );
457:     }
458: 
459:     fn self_test_mode() -> Result<()> {
460:         let job_name = format!(
461:             r"Local\PiDesktop.Managed.SelfTest.{:08x}",
462:             std::process::id()
463:         );
464:         let job = Job::create(&job_name)?;
465:         if job.active_processes()? != 0 {
466:             return Err(HelperError::protocol("JOB_QUERY_FAILED"));
467:         }
468:         println!(
469:             r#"{{"ok":true,"protocolVersion":{},"buildId":{},"arch":"x64","checks":["job-dacl","kill-on-close","completion-port","accounting"]}}"#,
470:             PROTOCOL_VERSION,
471:             super::protocol::json_escape(BUILD_ID),
472:         );
473:         Ok(())
474:     }
475: 
476:     pub fn run() -> i32 {
477:         let mode = std::env::args().nth(1);
478:         let _executable_lock = if matches!(
479:             mode.as_deref(),
480:             Some("--owner-stdio-v1") | Some("--reap-stdio-v1")
481:         ) {
482:             match win32::lock_current_executable() {
483:                 Ok(lock) => Some(lock),
484:                 Err(_) => return 2,
485:             }
486:         } else {
487:             None
488:         };
489:         if mode.as_deref() == Some("--version-json-v1") {
490:             version_mode();
491:             return 0;
492:         }
493:         if mode.as_deref() == Some("--self-test-json-v1") {
494:             return match self_test_mode() {
495:                 Ok(()) => 0,
496:                 Err(_) => 2,
497:             };
498:         }
499:         let sink = EventSink::start();
500:         if sink.send_json(HELPER_HELLO, hello()).is_err() {
501:             return 2;
502:         }
503:         let result = match mode.as_deref() {
504:             Some("--owner-stdio-v1") => owner_mode(&sink),
505:             Some("--reap-stdio-v1") => reaper_mode(&sink),
506:             _ => Err(HelperError::protocol("HELPER_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH")),
507:         };
508:         match result {
509:             Ok(()) => 0,
510:             Err(error) => {
511:                 let _ = sink.send_json(HELPER_ERROR, error_json(&error));
512:                 // Give the dedicated writer a bounded chance to emit the fixed
513:                 // diagnostic before process teardown closes the Job handle.
514:                 std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200));
515:                 2
516:             }
517:         }
518:     }
519: }

---
type: guide
title: Windows Managed Process Helper Guide
description: How the Windows x64 Rust helper provides Job Object containment for managed background processes, its frame protocol, build/reproducibility pipeline, integrity verification, and the acceptance gates that protect it.
tags: [windows, rust, managed-process, job-object, helper]
---

# Windows Managed Process Helper Guide

On Windows x64, managed background processes are contained by a small Rust binary, `pi-managed-process-helper.exe`, instead of the POSIX process-group mechanism used on macOS/Linux. It runs the target process inside a protected Job Object and is exercised both by the Agent Host (to spawn/control the process) and by Electron Main (to reap leftover jobs after a crash). This guide covers its protocol, build pipeline, integrity verification, and the gates that protect it.

## Responsibilities

The helper (`native/windows-managed-process-helper`) has fixed modes selected by the first CLI argument (`src/main.rs:476-518`):

- `--owner-stdio-v1` — owner mode: open owner handles, create the named Job, prepare a suspended target, assign it to the Job **before** resume with an inherited-handle allowlist, stream stdout/stderr, forward stdin, stop the process tree in graceful phases (CTRL_C → CTRL_BREAK → Job terminate), and terminate the Job if the owner/main identity is lost (`src/main.rs:252-401`).
- `--reap-stdio-v1` — reaper mode: either secure a journal directory or reap a named Job, verifying the helper's own identity by pid/start-fingerprint/build-id before touching it (`src/main.rs:403-448`).
- `--version-json-v1` and `--self-test-json-v1` — verification modes; the self-test validates `job-dacl`, `kill-on-close`, `completion-port`, and `accounting` (`src/main.rs:450-474`).

The helper must expose **no network surface** — owner/reaper/self-test/version modes only, with no `TcpListener`/`UdpSocket`/`std::net`/WinHttp code (`scripts/check-desktop-security.mjs:198-206`).

## Job containment invariants

The Win32 layer (`src/win32/mod.rs`) is gated by static security checks:

- the target is created `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, assigned to a `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` Job via `AssignProcessToJobObject`, then resumed — never with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` (`check-desktop-security.mjs:161-169`);
- named Jobs retain an exact protected current-user plus SYSTEM DACL (`JOB_OBJECT_TERMINATE | JOB_OBJECT_QUERY | READ_CONTROL | SYNCHRONIZE`, `PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION`), and reapers reopen the Job and verify the DACL before terminating (`check-desktop-security.mjs:170-177`);
- completion notifications are advisory: authoritative empty detection queries job accounting rather than relying on `GetQueuedCompletionStatus` (`check-desktop-security.mjs:178-183`);
- the cwd and shell executable are final-path verified against device namespaces before `CreateProcessW`, with shared read/write (not delete) handles (`check-desktop-security.mjs:184-196`);
- every `unsafe` block in the Win32 module must retain a `// SAFETY:` invariant and the count is pinned at 99 (`check-desktop-security.mjs:128-135`).

## Frame protocol

The helper speaks a bounded binary frame protocol over stdio (`src/protocol.rs`):

- a 16-byte header: magic `PIMP`, 2-byte protocol version (`1`), 2-byte kind, 4-byte length, 4-byte monotonic sequence that must advance exactly (`protocol.rs:56-113`);
- payload limits: bootstrap 512 KiB, control 128 KiB, output 64 KiB; oversized frames are rejected before allocation (`protocol.rs:5-8`, `protocol.rs:41-54`);
- JSON payloads are escaped safely (`json_escape`, `protocol.rs:157-178`);
- the same framing is mirrored on the TypeScript side by `WindowsHelperFrameDecoder`/`encodeWindowsHelperJson` in `src/agent-host/managed-process/helper-codec.ts` and consumed by the reaper (`src/main/managed-process/reaper.ts:119-207`).

## Build IDs and provenance

The build id is `pimpd-<app-version>-p<protocol>-<revision>`, where `revision` is a 12-hex SHA-256 digest over the build script, `.cargo/config.toml`, `build.rs`, `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `deny.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, and every file under `resources/` and `src/` (`scripts/build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:35-70`). Provenance is one of:

- `windows-native-dev` — a native Windows x64 build (`build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:205`);
- `release-authoritative` — the release build on Windows (`build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:205`);
- `cross-dev` — the cargo-xwin compile-only gate on macOS/Linux (`build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:159-161`).

The version resource embeds the tuple/version/build-id (`helper.rc.template`), and the build refuses to proceed unless the running `--version-json-v1` output matches exactly (`build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:233-253`).

## Build and packaging pipeline

`npm run build:windows-helper` → `scripts/build-windows-managed-helper.mjs`:

- **On Windows x64** it compiles the version resource with the pinned SDK's `rc.exe`, runs `cargo build --locked --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, verifies the PE, copies the exe to `out/native/windows-managed-process-helper/pi-managed-process-helper.exe`, runs `--version-json-v1` and `--self-test-json-v1`, and writes a `manifest.json` with the sha256 (`build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:197-291`).
- **On other platforms** it runs the compile-only cross gate: `cargo-xwin 0.23.1` with pinned LLVM 18, SDK `10.0.26100`, and CRT `14.44.17.14`, then verifies the PE (`build-windows-managed-helper.mjs:155-195`).
- `verifyWindowsHelperPe` (`scripts/windows-helper-pe.mjs:33-...`) enforces the PE shape: MZ/PE signature, x86-64, PE32+, subsystem 3, DLL characteristics `highEntropyVa | dynamicBase | nxCompat | guardCf`, and an import allowlist of exactly `advapi32.dll`, `api-ms-win-core-synch-l1-2-0.dll`, `kernel32.dll`, `ntdll.dll`, `user32.dll`.

Reproducibility is verified by `npm run check:windows-helper-reproducibility`, which builds twice with a targeted `cargo clean` between builds and requires identical sha256 (`scripts/verify-windows-helper-reproducibility.mjs:29-47`).

Supply chain: `Cargo.toml` pins `windows-sys = "=0.61.2"` with `panic = "abort"`, fat LTO, `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "deny"`, and clippy `-D warnings`; CI runs pinned `cargo-audit` and `cargo-deny` against the lockfile and `deny.toml`, and the crate must not use tokio/serde/reqwest/socket/tls (`Cargo.toml:8-34`, `check-desktop-security.mjs:118-127`).

## Integrity verification at runtime

`resolveWindowsManagedProcessHelper` (`src/shared/windows-managed-process-helper.ts:103-141`) is the fail-closed resolver used by Main at startup and update time:

- the helper directory is fixed: packaged `resources/managed-process/win32-x64`, dev `out/native/windows-managed-process-helper` (`windows-managed-process-helper.ts:109-111`);
- it requires an exact `manifest.json` schema and a sha256 of the executable matching the manifest; `--version-json-v1` output must also match unless verification is explicitly disabled (`windows-managed-process-helper.ts:43-101`, `:125-129`);
- any mismatch resolves to `HELPER_MISSING` or `HELPER_INTEGRITY` and the managed-process capability becomes not-ready (`contract/processes.ts:189-206`).

The executable is also locked against write/delete replacement while running (`lock_current_executable`), and update installation checks `verifyWindowsManagedProcessHelperReplaceable` before replacing the helper (`windows-managed-process-helper.ts:143-173`, `src/main/main.ts:463-474`). The reaper journal directory is secured through the helper itself (`secureWindowsReaperDirectory`, `src/main/managed-process/reaper.ts:41-117`).

## Acceptance tests

The helper is gated by Windows-only acceptance suites in CI (`scripts/test-windows-managed-process-helper.mjs`, plus the workflow steps in `build-desktop.yml`):

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`;
- `npm run check:windows-helper-reproducibility`;
- `npm run test:windows-managed-helper` with `PI_WINDOWS_HELPER_HANDLE_LOOPS=100`;
- `npm run test:managed-process-workflows` and the 60-second, eight-process dual-stream `test:managed-process-flood`;
- `npm run test:managed-process-frameworks` (real Next/Storybook/Spring Boot cold starts) and `npm run test:windows-nsis-upgrade` (hash-pinned previous NSIS upgrade, installed-helper locking, direct rollback).

## Related pages

- [Managed Background Processes](../systems/managed-processes.md)

claims.statement: The Windows helper exposes exactly four CLI modes: --owner-stdio-v1, --reap-stdio-v1, --version-json-v1, and --self-test-json-v1, with no network surface.

In owner mode the helper creates the named Job, prepares a suspended target, assigns it to the Job before resume, streams stdout/stderr, forwards stdin, stops the process tree in graceful phases (CTRL_C, CTRL_BREAK, then Job terminate), and terminates the Job if the owner identity is lost.

The Win32 layer creates the target suspended, assigns it to a JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE Job via AssignProcessToJobObject before ResumeThread with an inherited-handle allowlist, and never uses CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB.
Named Jobs retain an exact protected current-user plus SYSTEM DACL and reapers reopen the Job and verify the DACL (READ_CONTROL) before terminating.

The helper uses a 16-byte binary frame header (magic PIMP, protocol version 1, kind, length, monotonic sequence) over stdio, with payload limits of 512 KiB for bootstrap, 128 KiB for control, and 64 KiB for output, and oversized frames are rejected before allocation.

The helper build id is pimpd-<app-version>-p<protocol>-<revision>, where revision is a SHA-256 digest over the build script, cargo config, build.rs, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, deny.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, and every file under resources/ and src/.

verify-windows-helper-reproducibility builds the release helper twice with a targeted cargo clean between builds and fails unless the sha256 hashes match.

1: import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
2: import type {
3:   BrowserAdvancedRuntimePolicy,
4:   BrowserCapabilityLease,
5:   BrowserCapabilitySnapshot,
6:   BrowserHostRequestContext,
7:   BrowserPermissionLevel,
8:   BrowserSessionGrantInput,
9:   BrowserSettingsV2,
10: } from "../../contract/browser.ts";
11: import { BrowserError } from "./browser-error.ts";
12: 
13: const PERMISSION_RANK: Record<BrowserPermissionLevel, number> = {
14:   none: 0,
15:   read: 1,
16:   interact: 2,
17:   advanced: 3,
18: };
19: const DEFAULT_GRANT_TTL_MS = 8 * 60 * 60 * 1_000;
20: const DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1_000;
21: 
22: type SessionGrant = BrowserSessionGrantInput & { expiresAt: number };
23: 
24: export interface BrowserPolicyEngineOptions {
25:   now?: () => number;
26:   createId?: () => string;
27:   grantTtlMs?: number;
28:   leaseTtlMs?: number;
29: }
30: 
31: export class BrowserPolicyEngine {
32:   private revision = 0;
33:   private settings: BrowserSettingsV2;
34:   private readonly grants = new Map<string, SessionGrant>();
35:   private readonly leases = new Map<string, BrowserCapabilityLease>();
36:   private readonly listeners = new Set<(snapshot: BrowserCapabilitySnapshot) => void>();
37:   private readonly now: () => number;
38:   private readonly createId: () => string;
39:   private readonly grantTtlMs: number;
40:   private readonly leaseTtlMs: number;
41: 
42:   constructor(settings: BrowserSettingsV2, options: BrowserPolicyEngineOptions = {}) {
43:     this.settings = structuredClone(settings);
44:     this.now = options.now ?? Date.now;
45:     this.createId = options.createId ?? randomUUID;
46:     this.grantTtlMs = options.grantTtlMs ?? DEFAULT_GRANT_TTL_MS;
47:     this.leaseTtlMs = options.leaseTtlMs ?? DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_MS;
48:   }
49: 
50:   subscribe(listener: (snapshot: BrowserCapabilitySnapshot) => void): () => void {
51:     this.listeners.add(listener);
52:     listener(this.getSnapshot());
53:     return () => this.listeners.delete(listener);
54:   }
55: 
56:   getRevision(): number {
57:     return this.revision;
58:   }
59: 
60:   getSettings(): BrowserSettingsV2 {
61:     return structuredClone(this.settings);
62:   }
63: 
64:   getAdvancedRuntimePolicy(): BrowserAdvancedRuntimePolicy {
65:     const advanced = this.settings.advancedBrowserMode;
66:     if (!advanced.enabled) return createDisabledAdvancedRuntimePolicy();
67:     return {
68:       enabled: true,
69:       removeSiteSecurityHeaders: true,
70:       disableWebSecurity: true,
71:       allowInsecureContent: true,
72:       certificateBypassDomains: [...advanced.certificateBypassDomains],
73:       unrestrictedRawCdp: true,
74:     };
75:   }
76: 
77:   isAdvancedEnabled(): boolean {
78:     return this.settings.advancedBrowserMode.enabled;
79:   }
80: 
81:   isHighRiskPermissionEnabled(): boolean {
82:     return this.isAdvancedEnabled();
83:   }
84: 
85:   updateSettings(settings: BrowserSettingsV2): BrowserCapabilitySnapshot {
86:     this.settings = structuredClone(settings);
87:     if (!settings.enabled || !settings.automation.enabled) this.grants.clear();
88:     if (!settings.advancedBrowserMode.enabled) this.downgradeAdvancedGrants();
89:     this.bumpRevision();
90:     return this.getSnapshot();
91:   }
92: 
93:   grantSession(input: BrowserSessionGrantInput): BrowserCapabilityLease | undefined {
94:     const sessionId = validateSessionId(input.sessionId);
95:     if (!this.settings.enabled) throw new BrowserError("BROWSER_DISABLED", "The built-in browser is disabled");
96:     if (!this.settings.automation.enabled) {
97:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_DISABLED", "Agent browser tools are disabled");
98:     }
99:     if (input.source === "channel" && !this.settings.automation.allowChannelSessions) {
100:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_DISABLED", "Browser access for channel sessions is disabled");
101:     }
102:     if (input.permission === "advanced") {
103:       if (!this.isHighRiskPermissionEnabled()) {
104:         throw new BrowserError("ADVANCED_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED", "Advanced browser capabilities are disabled");
105:       }
106:     }
107:     const requestedTtl = input.expiresInMs ?? this.grantTtlMs;
108:     const ttl = Math.max(1_000, Math.min(requestedTtl, this.grantTtlMs));
109:     this.grants.set(sessionId, { ...input, sessionId, expiresAt: this.now() + ttl });
110:     this.bumpRevision();
111:     return input.permission === "none" ? undefined : this.issueLease(sessionId);
112:   }
113: 
114:   revokeSession(sessionId: string): BrowserCapabilitySnapshot {
115:     const normalized = validateSessionId(sessionId);
116:     this.grants.delete(normalized);
117:     for (const [id, lease] of this.leases) {
118:       if (lease.sessionId === normalized) this.leases.delete(id);
119:     }
120:     this.bumpRevision();
121:     return this.getSnapshot();
122:   }
123: 
124:   revokeAll(): BrowserCapabilitySnapshot {
125:     this.grants.clear();
126:     this.bumpRevision();
127:     return this.getSnapshot();
128:   }
129: 
130:   issueLease(sessionId: string): BrowserCapabilityLease {
131:     this.pruneExpired();
132:     const normalized = validateSessionId(sessionId);
133:     const grant = this.grants.get(normalized);
134:     if (!grant || grant.permission === "none") {
135:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_DISABLED", "This session has no Browser permission");
136:     }
137:     if (grant.permission === "advanced" && !this.isHighRiskPermissionEnabled()) {
138:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_DISABLED", "Advanced Browser permission is no longer enabled");
139:     }
140:     const lease: BrowserCapabilityLease = {
141:       id: this.createId(),
142:       sessionId: normalized,
143:       permission: grant.permission,
144:       policyRevision: this.revision,
145:       expiresAt: Math.min(grant.expiresAt, this.now() + this.leaseTtlMs),
146:     };
147:     this.leases.set(lease.id, lease);
148:     return structuredClone(lease);
149:   }
150: 
151:   getLeaseForSession(sessionId: string): BrowserCapabilityLease | undefined {
152:     this.pruneExpired();
153:     const normalized = validateSessionId(sessionId);
154:     const lease = [...this.leases.values()]
155:       .filter((candidate) => candidate.sessionId === normalized && candidate.policyRevision === this.revision)
156:       .sort((left, right) => right.expiresAt - left.expiresAt)[0];
157:     return lease ? structuredClone(lease) : undefined;
158:   }
159: 
160:   assertRequest(context: BrowserHostRequestContext, required: BrowserPermissionLevel): BrowserCapabilityLease {
161:     this.pruneExpired();
162:     if (!this.settings.enabled) throw new BrowserError("BROWSER_DISABLED", "The built-in browser is disabled");
163:     if (!this.settings.automation.enabled) {
164:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_DISABLED", "Agent browser tools are disabled");
165:     }
166:     if (!context.requestId || context.requestId.length > 256 || /[\0\r\n]/.test(context.requestId)) {
167:       throw new BrowserError("INVALID_BROWSER_REQUEST", "Browser requestId is invalid");
168:     }
169:     if (context.policyRevision !== this.revision) {
170:       throw new BrowserError("POLICY_REVISION_MISMATCH", "Browser policy changed; refresh capabilities", {
171:         retryable: true,
172:         details: { expectedRevision: this.revision },
173:       });
174:     }
175:     const lease = this.leases.get(context.capabilityLeaseId);
176:     if (!lease || lease.expiresAt <= this.now()) {
177:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_LEASE_EXPIRED", "Browser capability lease expired", { retryable: true });
178:     }
179:     if (lease.policyRevision !== this.revision || lease.sessionId !== context.sessionId) {
180:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_LEASE_EXPIRED", "Browser capability lease is no longer valid", {
181:         retryable: true,
182:       });
183:     }
184:     if (PERMISSION_RANK[lease.permission] < PERMISSION_RANK[required]) {
185:       throw new BrowserError("CAPABILITY_DISABLED", `Browser ${required} permission is required`);
186:     }
187:     if (required === "advanced" && !this.isHighRiskPermissionEnabled()) {
188:       throw new BrowserError("ADVANCED_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED", "Advanced browser capabilities are disabled");
189:     }
190:     return structuredClone(lease);
191:   }
192: 
193:   getSnapshot(): BrowserCapabilitySnapshot {
194:     this.pruneExpired();
195:     const sessionPermissions: Record<string, BrowserPermissionLevel> = {};
196:     for (const [sessionId, grant] of this.grants) sessionPermissions[sessionId] = grant.permission;
197:     return {
198:       revision: this.revision,
199:       browserEnabled: this.settings.enabled,
200:       automationEnabled: this.settings.automation.enabled,
201:       advancedEnabled: this.isHighRiskPermissionEnabled(),
202:       sessionPermissions,
203:       generatedAt: this.now(),
204:     };
205:   }
206: 
207:   private bumpRevision(): void {
208:     this.revision++;
209:     this.leases.clear();
210:     const snapshot = this.getSnapshot();
211:     for (const listener of this.listeners) listener(snapshot);
212:   }
213: 
214:   private pruneExpired(): void {
215:     const now = this.now();
216:     for (const [sessionId, grant] of this.grants) {
217:       if (grant.expiresAt <= now) this.grants.delete(sessionId);
218:     }
219:     for (const [id, lease] of this.leases) {
220:       if (lease.expiresAt <= now) this.leases.delete(id);
221:     }
222:   }
223: 
224:   private downgradeAdvancedGrants(): void {
225:     for (const [sessionId, grant] of this.grants) {
226:       if (grant.permission === "advanced") this.grants.set(sessionId, { ...grant, permission: "interact" });
227:     }
228:   }
229: }

237:     certificateBypassDomains: [],

245:     throw new BrowserError("INVALID_BROWSER_REQUEST", "Browser sessionId is invalid");
246:   }
247:   return normalized;
248: }

---
type: concept
title: Builtin Browser
description: The Main-owned WebContentsView browser shared by the user and the Agent: tabs and profiles, network policy and isolation, authorization and lease flow, capability gating, advanced mode, CDP, header rules, downloads, and snippets.
tags: [browser, webcontentsview, authorization, network, cdp, security]
---

# Builtin Browser

Pi Agent Desktop ships a full browser that the **user and the Agent share**: real Chromium pages run inside Main-owned `WebContentsView` instances, so remote web content never gets the app preload, Node, or the renderer bridge. The Agent can drive the same pages only through a per-session authorization flow, and Main preflights every tool request before any side effect.

## Ownership and layout

- The browser is owned by `BrowserService` (`src/main/browser/browser-service.ts`), which composes the policy engine, authorization coordinator, profile manager, tab manager, settings/restore/header/snippet stores, secret vault, network interceptors, and download managers. It is created in Main during startup and is reachable from the renderer via `piBridge.browser*` and from the Host via `browser.*` host requests (`src/main/main.ts:428-436`).
- Tabs are `WebContentsView` instances created sandboxed with `contextIsolation`, no Node integration, no `webviewTag`, and no preload bridge (`src/main/browser/browser-tab-manager.ts`, enforced by `check-desktop-security.mjs:579-587`). Each tab carries an `ownerSessionId` (null for user-only tabs), a profile, generation, control state, and crash state (`contract/browser.ts:266-285`).
- Browser sessions install permission request/check handlers and deny device permissions by default; a `setDevicePermissionHandler(() => false)` is required (`check-desktop-security.mjs:589-593`).

## Profiles

- `BrowserProfileManager` manages profiles backed by Electron sessions. The default profile `temporary` is ephemeral; users can create persistent profiles (stored in `browser-profiles.json`, capped at 16) and `unsafe` profiles used only by advanced mode (`src/main/browser/browser-profile-manager.ts:13-70`).
- Unsafe/advanced profiles must not be restored on startup (`contract/browser.ts:280-284`, tab-restoration checks).
- Persistent settings and stores live under the user data dir: `browser-settings.json` (settings), `browser-session-grants.json` (persistent grants), `browser-secrets.json` (encrypted secrets), `browser-tabs.json` (restore records), `browser-header-rules.json`, `browser-page-snippets.json` (`src/main/browser/browser-service.ts:97-148`).

## Network policy

`BrowserNetworkPolicy` checks every navigation URL before it is allowed (`src/main/browser/browser-network-policy.ts:63-128`):

- only `https:` and `http:` (plus `about:blank` when allowed); URLs with embedded credentials are blocked; plain HTTP requires `allowHttp` or user approval;
- private-network detection covers literal private hostnames/IPs and resolved addresses from the session resolver; `198.18/15` benchmarking addresses only count when a resolver in the same range exists and a PTR lookup confirms the hostname (virtual-DNS confirmation) (`browser-network-policy.ts:151-205`);
- private/local targets are blocked unless `allowPrivateNetwork` is set or the user approves; `strict` isolation is only honored when an enforcing network sandbox is available, otherwise the request fails with `NETWORK_ISOLATION_UNAVAILABLE` (`browser-network-policy.ts:96-101`). Private-network protection is explicitly **best-effort** without a controlled network sandbox.

## Agent authorization and leases

The Agent gains browser capabilities through a two-layer flow:

1. **Capability snapshot** — `BrowserPolicyEngine` publishes a revisioned `BrowserCapabilitySnapshot` (`browserEnabled`, `automationEnabled`, `advancedEnabled`, per-session permissions) to the Host, which mirrors it in `browserCapabilityRuntime` (`src/main/browser/browser-policy.ts:193-212`, `src/agent-host/browser-capability-runtime.ts:17-45`). Tool availability and session permission rank are evaluated against this snapshot.
2. **Authorization coordinator** — when a tool needs more than the current permission, `BrowserAuthorizationCoordinator.request` either grants from the persistent policy, or queues a dialog (`BrowserAgentAuthorizationRequest`) that the user resolves with `allow-session`/`deny`; denials impose a 2 s cooldown and requests time out after 60 s (`src/main/browser/browser-authorization-coordinator.ts:71-134`). Grants become session grants (8 h TTL) plus short-lived capability leases (15 min TTL) (`src/main/browser/browser-policy.ts:19-20`, `browser-policy.ts:93-149`).
3. **Main-side preflight** — every Host browser request carries `requestId`, `capabilityLeaseId`, and `policyRevision`; `BrowserPolicyEngine.assertRequest` validates them against the current revision and the lease, and enforces the required permission rank, before the action executes (`src/main/browser/browser-policy.ts:160-191`).

The Agent-side `browserCall` helper requests authorization via `browser.requestAuthorization` (70 s timeout), then re-reads capabilities before invoking the target method exactly once (`src/agent-host/browser-tools.ts:79-143`).

Tool-to-permission mapping is explicit: `browser_open`/`browser_snapshot`/`browser_inspect`/`browser_screenshot`/`browser_wait` are `read`; clicks/types/presses/scroll are `interact`; `browser_execute_javascript`, `browser_get_cookies`, CDP commands, network capture/replay, and page-code tools are `advanced` (`src/agent-host/browser-tools.ts:14-46`).

## Advanced browser mode

- Advanced mode is a single switch (`advancedBrowserMode.enabled`, default off) guarded by a one-time confirmation proof (`BrowserConfirmationManager`; settings updates consume the proof via `authorizeBrowserSettingsUpdate`) (`src/main/browser/browser-settings-confirmation.ts`, `browser-service.ts:230-259`).
- When enabled, the runtime policy removes site-security headers, disables web security, allows insecure content, permits the configured `certificateBypassDomains`, and allows unrestricted raw CDP; when disabled it returns a fully inert policy (`src/main/browser/browser-policy.ts:64-75`, `browser-policy.ts:231-240`).
- Advanced grants are downgraded to `interact` when advanced mode is disabled, and capability-boundary changes cancel pending authorizations and revoke all grants (`src/main/browser/browser-policy.ts:88`, `browser-service.ts:243-250`).

## Agent budgets and working memory

`BrowserAgentRuntime` (Host side) tracks per-session budgets and hashed working memory: 30 replan calls, 60 total calls, 8 screenshots, 4 exploratory and 2 verification JavaScript executions per turn; denied targets are stored as key/origin hashes, never plaintext (`src/agent-host/browser-agent-runtime.ts:5-60`). Browser tools expose canonical efficiency guidelines and label the workflow guard as "obvious-workflow-bypass-only" — it is lifecycle control, not an OS sandbox (`check-desktop-security.mjs:708-715`).

## Network capture, replay, and CDP

- `BrowserNetworkInterceptor`/`BrowserNetworkRecorder` capture bounded request/response bodies for `network_list`/`network_wait`/`network_body`/`network_summary` and **replay** confirmed write requests; replay data is sealed in Main memory with a 10-minute TTL (`src/main/browser/browser-network-recorder.ts`, `check-desktop-security.mjs:717-724`).
- `BrowserCdpCoordinator` brokers raw CDP for advanced mode; agent tools cannot accept cookie values and cookie mutation is unavailable until tool-result persistence isolation is proven (`check-desktop-security.mjs:648-653`).
- Inspection and Console output share redaction and bounded budgets (text ≤ 8 000 chars default, ≤ 100 nodes, screenshots ≤ 1.5 MB) (`check-desktop-security.mjs:682-694`).

## Downloads, uploads, and confirmation

- Downloads are managed per-tab by `BrowserDownloadManager` under the configured `downloads.mode` (`ask` / `deny` / `allow-to-directory`) (`contract/browser.ts:120-124`).
- Sensitive actions (cookies, form submission, external protocols, private-network access, route bypass) require a Main-side confirmation before proceeding; external protocols go through `openExternalWithConfirmation` (`src/main/browser/browser-service.ts:154-171`).

## Tab restore

- Tab restore records are persisted in `browser-tabs.json` and restored after startup (debounced 500 ms) unless the restore feature is disabled; unsafe/advanced-profile tabs are excluded from restoration (`src/main/browser/browser-service.ts:143`, `src/main/browser/browser-tab-restoration.ts`, `contract/browser.ts:92-98`).

## Related pages

- [Security Model](../architecture/security-model.md)
- [RPC and Contract Layer](../architecture/rpc-and-contracts.md)
- [Three-Process Architecture](../architecture/three-process-architecture.md)
- [Managed Background Processes](./managed-processes.md)

13:  * Small, injectable surface around electron-updater. Tests can implement this
14:  * interface without loading Electron or contacting an update server.
15:  */
16: export interface UpdateAdapter {
17:   on<Event extends keyof UpdateAdapterEventMap>(event: Event, listener: UpdateAdapterEventMap[Event]): () => void;
18:   checkForUpdates(): Promise<unknown>;
19:   downloadUpdate(): Promise<unknown>;
20:   cancelDownload?(): void;
21:   quitAndInstall(isSilent?: boolean, isForceRunAfter?: boolean): void;
22: }
23: 
24: type ElectronUpdaterModule = typeof import("electron-updater") & {
25:   default?: { autoUpdater?: AppUpdater };
26: };
27: 
28: export interface ProductionUpdateAdapterOptions {
29:   useDevelopmentConfig?: boolean;
30:   /** @internal Injectable so Node tests do not load electron-updater. */
31:   createCancellationToken?: () => CancellationToken;
32: }
33: 
34: export function isProductionUpdatePlatformEnabled(platform: NodeJS.Platform): boolean {
35:   // Windows releases intentionally omit publisherName while Authenticode
36:   // signing is unavailable. electron-updater therefore skips publisher
37:   // verification, but still validates the downloaded NSIS file against the
38:   // SHA-512 digest in latest.yml before running the interactive installer.
39:   return platform === "darwin" || platform === "win32";
40: }
41: 
42: class ProductionUpdateAdapter implements UpdateAdapter {
43:   private readonly updater: AppUpdater;
44:   private readonly createCancellationToken: (() => CancellationToken) | undefined;
45:   private activeDownloadToken: CancellationToken | null = null;
46: 
47:   constructor(updater: AppUpdater, createCancellationToken?: () => CancellationToken) {
48:     this.updater = updater;
49:     this.createCancellationToken = createCancellationToken;
50:   }
51: 
52:   on<Event extends keyof UpdateAdapterEventMap>(event: Event, listener: UpdateAdapterEventMap[Event]): () => void {
53:     // AppUpdater has strongly typed overloads, while this adapter exposes the
54:     // same callbacks through a generic event map.
55:     const updater = this.updater as unknown as {
56:       on(name: string, callback: (...args: never[]) => void): void;
57:       off(name: string, callback: (...args: never[]) => void): void;
58:     };
59:     const callback = listener as (...args: never[]) => void;
60:     updater.on(event, callback);
61:     return () => updater.off(event, callback);
62:   }
63: 
64:   checkForUpdates(): Promise<unknown> {
65:     return this.updater.checkForUpdates();
66:   }
67: 
68:   async downloadUpdate(): Promise<unknown> {
69:     const token = this.createCancellationToken?.() ?? null;
70:     this.activeDownloadToken = token;
71:     try {
72:       return await this.updater.downloadUpdate(token ?? undefined);
73:     } finally {
74:       if (this.activeDownloadToken === token) this.activeDownloadToken = null;
75:     }
76:   }
77: 
78:   cancelDownload(): void {
79:     this.activeDownloadToken?.cancel();
80:   }
81: 
82:   quitAndInstall(isSilent = false, isForceRunAfter = true): void {
83:     this.updater.quitAndInstall(isSilent, isForceRunAfter);
84:   }
85: }
86: 
87: /** @internal Exported to verify the production policy without loading Electron. */
88: export function wrapElectronUpdater(updater: AppUpdater, options: ProductionUpdateAdapterOptions = {}): UpdateAdapter {
89:   updater.autoDownload = false;
90:   // Installation must pass through UpdateManager.installUpdate(), which gates
91:   // active Agent sessions. App quit must never bypass that explicit check.
92:   updater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = false;
93:   updater.allowPrerelease = false;
94:   updater.allowDowngrade = false;
95:   updater.disableWebInstaller = true;
96:   updater.forceDevUpdateConfig = options.useDevelopmentConfig === true;
97: 
98:   // Avoid leaking request headers, URLs, or cache paths through the library's
99:   // default console logger. UpdateManager emits its own redacted messages.
100:   updater.logger = null;
101: 
102:   return new ProductionUpdateAdapter(updater, options.createCancellationToken);
103: }
104: 
105: /**
106:  * Loads electron-updater only when the packaged main process asks for it.
107:  * This keeps ordinary Node tests from initializing Electron's AppUpdater.
108:  */
109: export async function createProductionUpdateAdapter(
110:   options: ProductionUpdateAdapterOptions = {},
111: ): Promise<UpdateAdapter> {
112:   const imported = (await import("electron-updater")) as ElectronUpdaterModule;
113:   const updater = imported.autoUpdater ?? imported.default?.autoUpdater;
114:   if (!updater) {
115:     throw new Error("electron-updater did not expose autoUpdater");
116:   }
117:   return wrapElectronUpdater(updater, {
118:     ...options,
119:     createCancellationToken: () => new imported.CancellationToken(),
120:   });
121: }

2: import { app, dialog, shell, type BrowserWindow } from "electron";

10: 
11: const MAX_LOG_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;
12: const MAX_CRASH_METADATA_ENTRIES = 256;
13: 
14: export interface ExportDiagnosticsOptions {
15:   toolchainState?: PublicToolchainState;

19: export async function exportDiagnostics(
20:   win: BrowserWindow | null,
21:   options: ExportDiagnosticsOptions = {},
22: ): Promise<string | null> {
23:   const defaultName = `pi-desktop-diag-${new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, "-")}`;
24:   const result = await dialog.showSaveDialog(win ?? undefined!, {
25:     defaultPath: path.join(app.getPath("desktop"), defaultName),
26:     title: "Export diagnostics",
27:     properties: ["createDirectory", "showOverwriteConfirmation"],
28:   });
29:   if (result.canceled || !result.filePath) return null;
30: 
31:   const outDir = result.filePath;
32:   fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
33:   const roots = {
34:     homeDir: app.getPath("home"),
35:     userDataDir: app.getPath("userData"),
36:     logsDir: app.getPath("logs"),
37:     platform: process.platform,
38:   } as const;
39: 
40:   const info = {
41:     appVersion: app.getVersion(),
42:     electron: process.versions.electron,
43:     chrome: process.versions.chrome,
44:     node: process.versions.node,
45:     platform: process.platform,
46:     arch: process.arch,
47:     os: `${os.type()} ${os.release()}`,
48:     homedir: process.platform === "win32" ? "%USERPROFILE%" : "$HOME",
49:     userData: "<userData>",
50:     logs: "<logs>",
51:     exportedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
52:     privacy:
53:       "Logs are size-limited and redacted; environment variables, credentials, and raw crash dumps are excluded.",
54:   };
55:   writePrivateJson(path.join(outDir, "system.json"), info);
56:   if (options.toolchainState) {
57:     writePrivateJson(path.join(outDir, "toolchains.json"), buildToolchainDiagnosticSummary(options.toolchainState));
58:   }
59:   if (options.browser) writePrivateJson(path.join(outDir, "browser.json"), options.browser);
60: 
61:   await flushMainLog();
62:   const copiedNames = new Set<string>();
63:   copyRedactedLog(getMainLogPath(), "main.log", outDir, roots, copiedNames);
64:   try {
65:     for (const name of fs.readdirSync(roots.logsDir).sort()) {
66:       if (!name.toLowerCase().endsWith(".log")) continue;
67:       copyRedactedLog(path.join(roots.logsDir, name), path.basename(name), outDir, roots, copiedNames);
68:     }
69:   } catch {
70:     /* ignore unavailable log directories */
71:   }
72: 
73:   // Minidumps can contain process memory and credentials. Export metadata only;
74:   // a user can separately share a raw dump after reviewing that higher-risk file.
75:   const crashMetadata = collectCrashMetadata(app.getPath("crashDumps"));
76:   if (crashMetadata.length > 0) writePrivateJson(path.join(outDir, "crash-dumps.json"), crashMetadata);
77: 
78:   shell.showItemInFolder(outDir);
79:   return outDir;

81: 
82: function copyRedactedLog(
83:   source: string,
84:   destinationName: string,
85:   outDir: string,
86:   roots: Parameters<typeof redactDiagnosticText>[1],
87:   copiedNames: Set<string>,
88: ): void {

91:     const stat = fs.lstatSync(source);
92:     if (!stat.isFile() || stat.isSymbolicLink()) return;
93:     const content = readBoundedLog(source, stat.size);
94:     const redacted = redactDiagnosticText(content, roots);
95:     fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, destinationName), redacted, { encoding: "utf8", mode: 0o600 });
96:     copiedNames.add(destinationName);
97:   } catch {

99:   }
100: }
101: 
102: function readBoundedLog(filePath: string, size: number): string {
103:   if (size <= MAX_LOG_BYTES) return fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf8");
104:   const descriptor = fs.openSync(filePath, "r");
105:   try {
106:     const buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(MAX_LOG_BYTES);
107:     fs.readSync(descriptor, buffer, 0, buffer.length, size - buffer.length);
108:     return `[older log content omitted; original size ${size} bytes]\n${buffer.toString("utf8")}`;
109:   } finally {
110:     fs.closeSync(descriptor);
111:   }
112: }
113: 
114: function collectCrashMetadata(directory: string): Array<{ name: string; size: number; modifiedAt: string }> {
115:   try {
116:     const root = fs.lstatSync(directory);
117:     if (!root.isDirectory() || root.isSymbolicLink()) return [];
118:     return fs
119:       .readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true })
120:       .filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && !entry.isSymbolicLink())
121:       .slice(0, MAX_CRASH_METADATA_ENTRIES)
122:       .flatMap((entry) => {
123:         try {
124:           const stat = fs.lstatSync(path.join(directory, entry.name));
125:           return [{ name: entry.name, size: stat.size, modifiedAt: stat.mtime.toISOString() }];
126:         } catch {
127:           return [];
128:         }
129:       });
130:   } catch {
131:     return [];
132:   }
133: }
134: 
135: function writePrivateJson(filePath: string, value: unknown): void {
136:   fs.writeFileSync(filePath, `${JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)}\n`, { encoding: "utf8", mode: 0o600 });
137: }

---
type: concept
title: Desktop Shell and Lifecycle
description: The Electron Main shell: window creation and persisted state, application menus, tray and badges, single-instance lock, deep links, notifications, software updates, diagnostics export, crash recovery, and app:// serving.
tags: [main, window, tray, menu, updates, deep-link, diagnostics, lifecycle]
---

# Desktop Shell and Lifecycle

The Electron Main process acts as the desktop shell: it owns the window, menus, tray, notifications, deep links, software updates, diagnostics export, and crash recovery, while delegating agent work to the Host. This page covers the shell behaviors and lifecycle.

## Window creation and state

- `createMainWindow` (`src/main/window.ts:30-170`) builds the main `BrowserWindow` with `sandbox`, `contextIsolation`, no Node integration, and `webSecurity`, applying persisted bounds and maximization from the UI state, then loading the renderer entry (Vite URL in dev, `app://bundle/index.html` otherwise).
- Window bounds/position are persisted by `trackWindowState`, which debounces resize/move by 400 ms and saves on close into `ui-state.json` under the user data dir (`src/main/window-state.ts:40-70`). The state also carries theme, sidebar width, recent cwds, `backgroundMode`, and `automaticUpdateChecks` (`window-state.ts:8-21`).
- Close can hide to tray instead of quitting when `backgroundMode` is on (`src/main/main.ts:306-322`). `window.open` is denied and navigation is restricted to `app:` and the dev server (see [Three-Process Architecture](../architecture/three-process-architecture.md)).

## Menus

`installAppMenu` (`src/main/menu.ts:5-157`) builds a platform-aware menu: a macOS app menu with a Check for Updates item, File (New Session `CmdOrCtrl+N`, Switch Session `CmdOrCtrl+K`, Settings), Edit, View (developer roles only in dev), Window, and Help (Open Logs Folder, Export Diagnostics…, Check for Updates on Windows). Menu commands are forwarded to the renderer as `menu:*` IPC events, which the preload buffers one generation per fixed event so early navigation is not lost (`src/preload/preload.ts:37-53`).

## Tray and badges

- `createTray` shows a system tray icon; clicking it focuses/restores the window. The tooltip and menu surface the running session count and managed background-process count, and a "Stop All Background Processes" action appears while processes are running (`src/main/tray.ts:19-145`).
- Unread badges use `app.setBadgeCount` on macOS/Linux and a 16×16 overlay icon on the Windows taskbar (`src/main/main.ts:251-267`).
- The tray action for stopping all processes confirms with a warning dialog and calls `processes.stopAll` with a 15 s Host timeout (`src/main/main.ts:228-249`).

## Single instance and deep links

- `acquireSingleInstanceLock` calls `app.requestSingleInstanceLock`; a second instance instead focuses the existing window and passes its argv through `onSecondInstance` (`src/main/single-instance.ts:6-24`).
- The app registers the `pi-agent-desktop://` custom protocol (`src/main/main.ts:828-834`). `parseDesktopDeepLink` accepts `pi-agent-desktop://session/<id>` (hostname form) and `pi-agent-desktop:///session/<id>` path form; `handleDeepLink` forwards the session id to the renderer as `deep-link:session`, or queues it until a window exists (`src/main/deep-link.ts:3-23`, `main.ts:269-281`). macOS `open-url` is handled the same way (`main.ts:294-297`).

## Notifications

Main shows desktop notifications for background session completion (`agent-end`) with a click-through to the session, and for an available update when the window is hidden or unfocused (`src/main/main.ts:723-743`, `main.ts:524-544`). Notifications increment the unread badge for completed background sessions.

## Software updates

- `UpdateManager` (`src/main/update-manager.ts`) drives the state machine with phases `disabled`/`idle`/`checking`/`up-to-date`/`available`/`downloading`/`downloaded`/`installing`/`error` and typed error codes (`contract/desktop.ts:44-74`). Automatic checks start after 60 s and repeat every 6 h with 8% jitter, with a 15-minute download watchdog (`update-manager.ts:4-7`).
- The updater is gated to `darwin` and `win32` in production (or a dev test mode) and only exists in packaged builds (`src/main/main.ts:438-452`). Install is blocked while agent sessions are running; `prepareToInstall` stops managed processes within a hard deadline and verifies the Windows helper is replaceable before update installation, while `recoverFromInstallFailure` restarts the Host if installation fails (`src/main/main.ts:458-483`).
- `createProductionUpdateAdapter` wraps `electron-updater` with `autoDownload`, `autoInstallOnAppQuit`, `allowPrerelease`, and `allowDowngrade` all false, `disableWebInstaller` true, and a nulled logger; the renderer updater contract exposes only fixed actions and cannot configure a feed (`src/main/update-adapter.ts:88-103`, `check-desktop-security.mjs:525-544`).
- Updates are downloaded only after user confirmation, installed after the current tasks finish, and the client uses only the packaged app's fixed GitHub release configuration.

## Diagnostics export

`exportDiagnostics` (`src/main/diagnostics.ts:19-80`) writes, into a user-selected directory with `0700` permissions:

- `system.json` (version/platform info, privacy statement) and redacted `toolchains.json`/`browser.json` summaries;
- bounded, redacted copies of `main.log` and the app log directory (5 MiB cap, tail read for larger logs, `0600` files);
- crash metadata only — minidumps can contain process memory and credentials, so raw dumps are excluded by design (`diagnostics.ts:73-76`, `diagnostics.ts:114-133`).

Redaction is performed by `redactDiagnosticText` (see [Security Model](../architecture/security-model.md)).

## Crash recovery

- `RendererCrashRecovery` (`src/main/renderer-crash-recovery.ts:15-51`) bounds renderer reloads after `render-process-gone`: exponential backoff from 250 ms to 4 s, at most 3 reloads in a 60 s window, then a crash page. `oom`, `launch-failed`, and `integrity-failure` halt immediately; `clean-exit`/`killed` are ignored.
- A `--validate-packaged-startup` probe mode and a packaged cleanup-fault validation write reports into the user data dir and exit with a non-zero code on failure (`src/main/main.ts:51-52`, `main.ts:108-166`).
- Host crashes are handled by `HostManager` (heartbeat + bounded restarts); the renderer reconnects over a fresh MessagePort after a restart (see [Agent Host Runtime](../architecture/agent-host-runtime.md)).

## app:// protocol serving

`handleAppProtocol` serves the built renderer over the privileged `app://` scheme with a strict CSP and path containment, and serves user HTML previews under `app://preview/<token>/...` with a much narrower CSP, 30-minute TTL, and bounded assets (see [Security Model](../architecture/security-model.md) and `src/main/protocol.ts:154-251`).

## Related pages

- [Three-Process Architecture](../architecture/three-process-architecture.md)
- [Development and Verification Guide](../guides/development-and-verification.md)
- [Agent Host Runtime](../architecture/agent-host-runtime.md)

36:   private readonly maxBytes: number;
37:   private readonly maxRecords: number;
38:   private records: ManagedProcessLogRecord[] = [];
39:   private head = 0;
40:   private nextSeq = 1;
41:   private bytes = 0;
42:   private droppedBytes = 0;
43:   private droppedRecords = 0;

45:   constructor(

73:     if (!record) return false;
74:     this.head += 1;

168:   decoder: StringDecoder;
169:   line: string;
170:   retainedBytes: number;
171:   omittedBytes: number;
172:   carriageReturn: boolean;
173: };

175: export class ManagedProcessOutputDecoder {

177:   private readonly onEncodingWarning?: () => void;
178:   private decodedCharacters = 0;
179:   private replacementCharacters = 0;
180:   private encodingWarningSent = false;

183:     stderr: this.createState(),
184:   };

200:           if (character === "\uFFFD") this.replacementCharacters += 1;
201:         }
202:       }
203:       if (

205:         this.replacementCharacters >= 4 &&
206:         this.replacementCharacters * 10 >= this.decodedCharacters

210:       }
211:     }

213:   }

215:   end(stream: "stdout" | "stderr"): void {
216:     const state = this.states[stream];

222:     return { decoder: new StringDecoder("utf8"), line: "", retainedBytes: 0, omittedBytes: 0, carriageReturn: false };
223:   }

225:   private consume(stream: "stdout" | "stderr", state: DecoderState, value: string): void {
226:     let offset = 0;
227:     while (offset < value.length) {
228:       if (state.carriageReturn) {
229:         state.carriageReturn = false;
230:         if (value[offset] === "\n") {
231:           this.flush(stream, state);
232:           offset += 1;
233:           continue;
234:         }
235:         state.line = "";
236:         state.retainedBytes = 0;
237:         state.omittedBytes = 0;
238:       }

240:       const carriageReturn = value.indexOf("\r", offset);
241:       const lineFeed = value.indexOf("\n", offset);

250:         continue;

253:     }

262:       state.retainedBytes += segmentBytes;
263:       return;

267:       return;
268:     }

270:     let retainedBytes = 0;
271:     let omittedBytes = 0;
272:     for (const character of segment) {
273:       const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(character, "utf8");

276:         retainedBytes += bytes;

281:     state.line += retained;
282:     state.retainedBytes += retainedBytes;
283:     state.omittedBytes += omittedBytes;
284:   }

286:   private flush(stream: "stdout" | "stderr", state: DecoderState): void {
287:     const suffix = state.omittedBytes > 0 ? ` <line truncated: ${state.omittedBytes} bytes>` : "";

290:     state.retainedBytes = 0;
291:     state.omittedBytes = 0;
292:     state.carriageReturn = false;
